title: Enterprise Onboarding: Support, Integration, Escalation, Known Issues & QBR Playbook
author: Avery Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook consolidates the canonical customer-success and support procedures we use for enterprise onboarding at Redwood Inference. It combines the onboarding checklist, integration guidance, escalation playbook, known issues & workarounds, and the standard health-check / QBR materials into a single reference for CSMs, Solutions Engineers, Support, and Engineering.

Scope: Applies to all enterprise customers (Dedicated and Private plans) during onboarding through the first 90 days of production. Use this document as the baseline; specific customers may have supplements in their account playbooks.

Quick summary of owners
- Primary owner: Customer Success (CSM)
- Integration & pre-sales technical owner: Solutions Engineering (SE)
- Support escalation path: Support L1 -> L2 (SRE/Platform) -> L3 (Serving Runtime / Model Onboarding)
- Executive QBR owner: Customer Success Director

Contents
1) Onboarding phases and checklist
2) Integration guide (typical checklist and examples)
3) Escalation playbook (thresholds, contacts, procedure)
4) Known issues & workarounds (high-impact items)
5) Support process, SLAs, and severity definitions
6) Health checks & QBR template and metrics

1) Onboarding phases and checklist
Phase A – Pre-Kickoff (CSM/SE)
- Complete intake form: product scope, data residency, compliance needs, expected RPS and p99 latency targets, model family preference.
- Identify stakeholders: technical lead, security/compliance contact, procurement, executive sponsor.
- Provision initial account and role-based access (RBAC) using onboarding-template-iam.
- Schedule kickoff call and technical deep-dive.

Phase B – Kickoff (Week 0)
- Agenda: goals, success criteria (performance, cost, stability), timeline, integration approach, and risk plan.
- Deliverables: kickoff notes, agreed SLOs, and access matrix.

Phase C – Integration (Week 1–4)
- SE leads integration: example app setup, SDK walkthrough, auth (API keys or mTLS), network connectivity for Dedicated/Private (VPC peering / Transit Gateway).
- Provide sample prompts and traffic profile (session length, concurrency).
- Validate tokenization and prompt formatting with customer-specific test prompts.
- Enable observability hooks: tracing, per-route latency metrics, and sample logging config.

Phase D – Validation & Load Test (Week 2–6)
- Run functional tests, token-level cost validation, and performance/load test to customer RPS.
- Validate fallback policies and rollouts (canary or A/B as requested).
- Mitigate failures and tune batching/quantization configs with SE recommendation.

Phase E – Handover to Support & Production Launch (Week 4–12)
- Finalize runbooks, SLOs, escalation contacts, and post-launch monitoring dashboards.
- Schedule 30/60/90-day health checks and a 90-day QBR.

Minimum onboarding checklist (CSM/SE)
- [ ] Intake form completed
- [ ] Kickoff held and notes published
- [ ] Integration keys and network established
- [ ] Observability configured (traces, metrics, logs)
- [ ] Performance/load tests completed
- [ ] Known issues reviewed and mitigation plan in place
- [ ] Handover meeting scheduled with Support & SRE

2) Integration guide (typical checklist and examples)
Network and auth
- Dedicated/Private: confirm VPC CIDR, subnet mapping, NAT/egress rules, and KMS/HSM endpoints if applicable.
- Hosted: ensure IP allowlist and API key distribution is configured.
- For mTLS: exchange certs and confirm cipher suites.

SDK and client integration
- Provide quickstart (Node/Python/Go) snippets and repo links.
- Example Node pseudocode for request with streaming:
  const resp = await redwoodClient.chat.stream({ model: 'r-instruct-1', messages });
- Recommend embedding-based retrieval guidance if customer uses embeddings for search.

Observability and tracing
- Required hooks: per-request ID, user ID (hashed), route name, model version.
- Metrics to enable: token_count, request_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), inference_errors, model_fallback_count, cache_hit_rate.
- Provide Grafana dashboard template and link to dashboard provisioning playbook.

Data handling and compliance
- Confirm data residency and retention window. For Private deployments, confirm site-local logging endpoints and compliance evidence requirements (SOC2, ISO).
- Recommended redaction: PII patterns, secrets, and long transcripts.

Common integration pitfalls and fixes
- Symptom: high p99 latency on short requests. Fix: enable smaller batch sizes or dedicated low-latency pool.
- Symptom: tokenization mismatch (unexpected token count). Fix: synchronize tokenizer model and encoding library versions.
- Symptom: frequent model fallbacks. Fix: pin compatible model version or increase capacity for chosen region.

3) Escalation playbook (thresholds, contacts, procedure)
Severity definitions
1. Sev1 (Critical) – Production outage impacting all users or significant data loss. Target response: 15 minutes.
2. Sev2 (High) – Large portion of users impacted, severe degradation (p99 >> SLO). Target response: 60 minutes.
3. Sev3 (Medium) – Partial impact, feature degraded. Target response: 4 business hours.
4. Sev4 (Low) – Informational requests, configuration assistance. Target response: 24 business hours.

Escalation steps
1) Triage (Support L1)
- Verify customer identity and scope of impact.
- Collect telemetry: request IDs, timestamps, route names, model version, API keys used, recent deploys.
- Reproduce in staging/private repro environment if possible.
- If Sev1/Sev2, page SRE and SE via PagerDuty channel: redwood-sev-pager.

2) Engage (Support L2/SRE)
- Run prebuilt runbook for suspected subsystem: networking, quota, model-serving, or database.
- Check per-region capacity queues, GPU pool saturation, and autoscaler events.
- For model regressions, check recent model rollout logs and fallback counts.

3) Escalate to engineering (Support L3 / Eng serving runtime)
- Include timeline, reproduction steps, request traces, and any dump logs.
- If root cause requires code change or hotfix, open a fast-track PR with priority label and include a rollback plan.

4) Customer communications and status updates
- Provide updates every 30 minutes for Sev1 until resolved.
- Document timeline in the incident/issue ticket and prepare post-incident notes.

Contacts and channels
- Primary support channel: support.redwood.com ticketing system (link in account notes).
- Pager: redwood-sev-pager (only for Sev1/Sev2).
- Slack: #support-enterprise (for asynchronous coordination).
- CSM escalation: CSM on-call list maintained in team roster.

4) Known issues & workarounds (high-impact items)
Format: Issue | Impact | Workaround | Owner
- Tokenization drift after model upgrade | Incorrect token counts and cost mismatch | Pin tokenizer version, run token count validation script; roll back if necessary | SE/Model-Onboarding
- Intermittent GPU OOM during peak batching | Requests fail with OOM on high-concurrency bursts | Reduce batch size, enable per-request max_tokens limit, schedule burst capacity | SRE/Serving Runtime
- Private deployment network MTU mismatch | Large payloads stall or time out | Confirm and set MTU to 9001 in VPC configuration; provide sample iperf test | Eng-Private-Deployments
- Observability ingestion lag on high-volume customers | Dashboards show stale metrics (>2 min lag) | Increase metrics ingestion lag buffer, enable sampling, or use direct log-forwarder | Eng-Platform
- Model fallback oscillation after autoscaler events | Increased latency and degraded responses | Stabilize autoscaler policies, add cooldown window, or pin to dedicated capacity | SRE/Runtime

(For each item above, there is a linked per-issue runbook. See related_pages.)

5) Support process, SLAs, and severity definitions
SLA targets (default enterprise)
- Availability: 99.9% uptime for hosted API, 99.95% for Dedicated with SLA clause.
- Response targets: Sev1 15 min, Sev2 60 min, Sev3 4 hours, Sev4 24 hours (business hours).
- Resolution target guidance: Sev1 within 6 hours (temporary mitigation), full remediation planned and scheduled within 72 hours.

Support workflow
1. Customer opens ticket (support portal or email).
2. L1 acknowledges and collects telemetry within response SLA.
3. If L1 cannot resolve, escalate to L2 with full context.
4. L2 either resolves or escalates to Eng L3.
5. Upon resolution, L2/CSM runs root-cause analysis entry and schedules postmortem for Sev1/Sev2.

Ticket tagging and metadata (required on every enterprise ticket)
- customer_id, environment (prod/staging), deployment_type (hosted/dedicated/private), model_version, sla_tier, CSM_name.

6) Health checks & QBR template and metrics
Cadence and owners
- 30-day health check: CSM + SE (operational readiness)
- 60-day health check: CSM + SRE + SE (performance & stability)
- 90-day QBR: CSM + Customer Executive Sponsor + Solutions Engineering + Product (as required)

Standard health metrics to review
- Adoption: active_users, daily_requests, growth_rate_30d
- Performance: p50/p95/p99 latency by route, error_rate, model_fallback_rate
- Cost & efficiency: avg_tokens_per_request, cost_per_1k_tokens, cache_hit_rate, batching_efficiency
- Reliability: uptime, incident_count_last_90d, MTTR per incident
- Security & compliance: audit_log_uptime, number_of_privileged_changes, outstanding_compliance_items

Sample 90-day QBR agenda (60 minutes)
1) Welcome & agenda (5m) – CSM
2) Business outcomes & adoption highlights (10m) – Customer + CSM
3) Performance & reliability review (15m) – SRE/SE
4) Cost & optimization opportunities (10m) – CSM/Optimize team
5) Roadmap & feature requests (10m) – Product
6) Action items, owners, and timelines (10m) – CSM

QBR deliverables
- One-page health summary with top 3 wins, top 3 risks, prioritized action items, and target owners.
- Dashboard snapshot exports (last 90 days) for the metrics above.
- Follow-up timeline with owners and due dates.

Appendices
A. Example runbook excerpt for high memory OOM (quick steps)
1) Identify offending requests using request_id and trace.
2) If on Dedicated/GPU pool: check node usage, kill/queue large batched jobs.
3) Apply temporary throttling or reduce batch sizes.
4) If caused by model change, roll back to previous model version and open model investigation ticket.

B. Integration CLI snippets
- Generate API key: redwoodctl keys create --name "customer-integration" --expiry 90d
- Provision dashboard: redwoodctl dashboards apply --file customer-dashboard.json

C. Links and references
- Support portal: https://support.redwood.com
- Internal runbook index: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks
- Onboarding intake form template: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/onboarding-intake-template

D. Revision history
- 2025-09-10: Initial draft (Avery Chen)
- 2025-11-04: Added Known Issues section and sample runbooks (Maya Singh)
- 2026-03-05: Updated SLAs, QBR template, and escalation contacts (Jordan Patel)

If you are a CSM, SE, or Support engineer preparing for a customer kickoff: copy this page into the customer folder, complete the onboarding checklist, link the customer dashboards, and confirm the owners for each action item before the kickoff meeting.
